date_note: The press release gives only its publication day.
title: RH-ISAC expects familiar fraud to arrive through AI-driven traffic this holiday season
summary: RH-ISAC's 2026 Holiday Threat Trends report assesses, with moderate confidence, that the largest agentic commerce risk this season comes from existing fraud types: card testing, account takeover and checkout page card theft. RH-ISAC says these will be delivered through a growing volume of AI-driven web traffic.
plain: A retail security group says the main holiday risk from AI shopping agents is familiar fraud, such as card testing and account takeover, arriving through more AI-driven web traffic.
exec: RH-ISAC assesses with moderate confidence that existing fraud types, delivered via AI-driven traffic, are the largest agentic commerce risk this season.
action: RH-ISAC advises classifying AI agent traffic and enforcing policy on it, strengthening card-testing and account takeover controls, checking checkout pages for injected third-party scripts, and sharing observations with RH-ISAC.

validation.note: RH-ISAC's own press release; the report itself was not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, moderate-confidence assessment, fraud types and advice with RH-ISAC press release
